title: Angles: Acute, Right, Obtuse, Straight, Reflex and Revolution
seo_title: Grade 5 Angles Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise, describe, name and compare angles in 2-D shapes, including acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex and revolution; estimate and compare angles with a right angle.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 5 angles worksheets: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex and revolution, estimating and angles in shapes. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Compare every angle with a right angle.
key_sub: Acute < right < obtuse < straight < reflex < revolution.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A right angle is a quarter turn (90°).
  • Acute: smaller than a right angle. Obtuse: bigger than a right angle, smaller than a straight angle.
  • Straight angle: half a turn (180°). Reflex: bigger than a straight angle. Revolution: a full turn (360°).
  • The size of an angle is the amount of turn, not the length of the arms.

Examples

Example

An angle of 250°

more than 180°

less than 360°

Answer: a reflex angle

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Long arms, big angleLook at the turn, not the arms.
Obtuse or reflex?Reflex is more than a straight angle.
A straight lineIt is a straight angle of 180°.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 5 say about angles?
faq.a: Recognise, describe and name angles: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex and revolution, and estimate and compare angles with a right angle.

faq.q: How big is a straight angle?
What angle do the hands make at 3 o'clock?

items.q: What type of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 35°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 125°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 230°. (The angle on the other side is 130°, but the arc marks the big angle.)

items.q: What type of angle is marked?
items.e: A right angle is exactly 90°, a quarter turn. The small square shows it. This angle is 90°. Turning the angle does not change its size.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 320°. (The angle on the other side is 40°, but the arc marks the big angle.)
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 160°.

items.q: What type of angle is marked?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 70°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 200°. (The angle on the other side is 160°, but the arc marks the big angle.)
Two arms that make a straight line make an angle of 180°, half a turn. This angle is 180°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 100°.

items.q: An angle measures 175°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight line. 175° is more than 90° but less than 180°.

items.q: An angle measures 185°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line. 185° is more than 180° but less than 360°.

items.q: An angle measures 89°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle. 89° is less than 90° (only just!).

items.q: An angle measures 270°. What type of angle is it?
items.e: A reflex angle is bigger than a straight line. 270° is more than 180° but less than 360°.

items.q: Which of these angles is reflex?
items.e: A reflex angle is more than 180°. Only 210° is more than 180°. 175° is close to 180°, but it is still obtuse.

items.q: Which of these angles is obtuse?
items.e: An obtuse angle is between 90° and 180°. 135° is the only one. 225° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.

items.q: A reflex angle is …
items.e: Reflex angles are bigger than a half turn (180°) but smaller than a whole turn (360°).

items.q: Lerato says an angle of 190° is obtuse because it is bigger than 90°. Is she right?
c: No, it is a right angle
items.e: Obtuse angles are bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°. 190° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest angle to the largest?
items.e: Acute is less than 90°, a right angle is 90°, obtuse is between 90° and 180°, and reflex is more than 180°.

items.q: At which time is the smaller angle between the hands of a clock acute?
items.e: At 1 o’clock the hands are 1 hour space apart: 30°, which is acute. 3 o’clock is a right angle (90°), 4 o’clock is obtuse (120°) and 6 o’clock is a straight line (180°).

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 35°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 125°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 230°. (The gap between the arms is 130°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: A right angle is exactly 90°, a quarter turn. The small square shows it. Turning the angle does not change its size or its name.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 320°. (The gap between the arms is 40°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 160°.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 70°.
A straight angle is exactly 180°, half a turn. The two arms make a straight line.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 200°. (The gap between the arms is 160°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)
A revolution is one whole turn: exactly 360°. The arm turns all the way round and ends where it started.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 100°.
A straight angle is exactly 180°, half a turn. The two arms make a straight line. Turning the angle does not change its size or its name.

items.q: An angle measures 175°. What is its name?
items.e: 175° is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse. It is close to a straight angle, but not 180°.

items.q: An angle measures 185°. What is its name?
items.e: 185° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is reflex, even though it is close to a straight angle.

items.q: An angle measures 89°. What is its name?
items.e: 89° is less than 90°, so it is acute (only just). A right angle is exactly 90°.

items.q: An angle measures 270°. What is its name?
items.e: 270° is more than 180° but less than 360°, so it is reflex. It is three right angles: 3 × 90° = 270°.

items.q: An angle measures 360°. What is its name?
items.e: 360° is one whole turn: a revolution. A straight angle is only half a turn (180°).

items.q: How many degrees are in a revolution?
items.e: A revolution is one whole turn: 360°. It is 4 right angles: 4 × 90° = 360°. 180° is a straight angle, only half a turn.

items.q: Tshepo says an angle of 190° is obtuse because it is bigger than 90°. Is he right?
items.e: Obtuse angles are bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°. 190° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.

items.q: Nadia says an angle of 190° is obtuse because it is bigger than 90°. Is she right?
items.e: Obtuse angles are bigger than 90° but smaller than 180°. 190° is more than 180°, so it is reflex.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 30° fits. (It is 28°.) About 150° would be a much wider angle.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 60° fits. (It is 62°.) About 120° would be a much wider angle.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°), so it is obtuse. About 120° fits. (It is 118°.) About 60° would be a much smaller angle.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°), so it is obtuse. About 150° fits. (It is 147°.) About 30° would be a much smaller angle.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 45° fits. (It is 43°.) About 135° would be a much wider angle.
The angle is bigger than a right angle (90°) but smaller than a straight line (180°), so it is obtuse. About 170° fits. (It is 172°.) About 10° would be a much smaller angle.
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 120°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 120° = 240°. (It is 235°.)
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 60°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 60° = 300°. (It is 300°.)
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 160°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 160° = 200°. (It is 205°.)
The arc goes round the outside, so the angle is reflex: more than 180°. The angle on the other side is about 90°, so the marked angle is about 360° − 90° = 270°. (It is 275°.)

items.q: Use benchmark angles. Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is less than half a right angle (45°). About 30° fits. (150° is what the outer scale of a protractor would say.)

items.q: Use benchmark angles. Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is about half of a right angle, so it is about 45°.

items.q: Use benchmark angles. Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle is more than half a right angle (45°) but less than a right angle (90°). About 60° fits.

items.q: Use benchmark angles. Which is the best estimate for the marked angle?
items.e: The angle looks like a square corner, so it is about 90°. (It is 88°.)
The angle is a bit more than a right angle (90°), but less than 135°. About 120° fits. (60° would be acute.)
The angle is about halfway between a right angle (90°) and a straight angle (180°), so it is about 135°.
The angle is more than 135° but less than a straight angle (180°). About 150° fits. (30° is the acute angle on the other side.)
The arms almost make a straight line (180°), so the angle is about 170°. (10° is the small gap left to make a straight line.)

items.q: Which angle is closest to 45°?
items.e: 45° is half a right angle. B is about half of a square corner. A is nearly a right angle, C is very small and D is obtuse.
120° is a bit more than a right angle, but less than 135°. C fits. A is acute, B is nearly straight and D is only just more than a right angle.

c: Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the angles are not all equal
items.e: All 6 sides have the same mark and all 6 angles have the same mark. Equal sides and equal angles: regular.

c: Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the angles are not all equal
items.e: All 4 sides are equal, but the angles are 60° and 120°. A regular polygon needs equal sides and equal angles, so this rhombus is irregular.

items.q: The marks show which sides and angles are equal. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: the angles are not all equal
Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
items.e: All 4 angles are right angles, but the long sides and the short sides are different. Equal angles are not enough, so this rectangle is irregular.

items.q: Is this pentagon regular or irregular?
c: Regular: all sides and all angles are equal
Irregular: the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides and the angles are not all equal
Irregular: the sides are not all equal
items.e: There are no equal marks. The sides are clearly different lengths and the angles are different sizes, so it is irregular.

items.q: A shape has 4 equal sides. Must it be a regular polygon?
c: Yes, all its sides are equal
No, its angles must be equal too
items.e: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal. A rhombus has 4 equal sides but its angles can be different.

items.q: Which shape is always a regular polygon?
items.e: An equilateral triangle always has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles (60° each). A rectangle, a rhombus or a hexagon can be irregular.

items.q: Naledi draws a hexagon. All its angles are 120°, but some sides are 3 cm and some are 5 cm. Is it regular?
c: No, the angles are not all equal
No, the sides are not all equal
Yes, the angles are all equal
items.e: Regular needs equal angles and equal sides. The sides are 3 cm and 5 cm, so the hexagon is irregular.

items.q: A regular octagon has a perimeter of 48 cm. How long is each side?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides. 48 ÷ 8 = 6 cm.

items.q: A regular pentagon has one angle of 108°. What is the size of each of its other angles?
items.e: In a regular polygon all the angles are equal, so every angle is 108°.

items.q: What is the smaller angle between the hands of the clock at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 hour spaces go around 360°, so each is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: At 4 o’clock the smaller angle between the hands of a clock is 120°. What is the reflex angle between the hands?
items.e: The two angles between the hands go all the way round: 360°. 360° − 120° = 240°. (60° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: 12 to 3, 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 are three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°. (90° is the short way, from 9 to 12.)

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand of a clock turn in 15 minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes is a whole turn (360°). 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, so a quarter turn: 90°.

items.q: A reflex angle and an angle of 85° fit together to make a whole turn. What is the reflex angle?
items.e: A whole turn is 360°. 360° − 85° = 275°. (95° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: Jabu faces east in the playground. He turns 90° anticlockwise. Which way does he face now?
items.e: Anticlockwise from east, a quarter turn takes you to north. (Clockwise would be south.)

items.q: A robot faces north. It turns through 3 right angles clockwise. Which way does it face now?
items.e: Clockwise from north: east (1 right angle), south (2), west (3). (East would be 3 right angles anticlockwise.)

items.q: A windmill sail turns a half turn and then a quarter turn more. How many degrees does it turn altogether?
items.e: A half turn is 180° and a quarter turn is 90°. 180° + 90° = 270°.

items.q: Daniel measures an angle and writes 40°. The angle is clearly bigger than a right angle. What should he have written?
items.e: An angle bigger than a right angle is more than 90°. Daniel read the wrong scale: the other scale gives 180° − 40° = 140°.

items.q: Three paths meet at a point. Two of the angles between them are 90° and 150°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The three angles go all the way around the point: 360°. 90° + 150° = 240°, and 360° − 240° = 120°.

items.q: Mbali cuts a round cake into 4 equal slices from the centre. What angle does each slice make at the centre?
items.e: The slices go all the way round the centre: 360°. 360° ÷ 4 = 90°, a right angle. (45° comes from using 180°.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 spaces between the numbers go round a revolution, 360°, so each space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle between the hands at 3 o’clock?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands are 3 spaces apart: 3 × 30° = 90°. That is a right angle, a quarter turn.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle between the hands at 5 o’clock?
items.e: At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. That is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: At 6 o’clock the hands of an analogue clock point in opposite directions. What angle do they make?
items.e: 6 spaces × 30° = 180°. The hands make one straight line: a straight angle, half a turn. (A revolution would be a whole turn, 360°.)

items.q: At 8 o’clock the smaller angle between the hands is 120°. What is the reflex angle between the hands?
items.e: The two angles between the hands make a revolution: 360°. 360° − 120° = 240°. (60° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: In one hour the minute hand turns all the way round once. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: All the way round once is a revolution: 360°. (180° is only half a turn, from 12 to 6.)

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn in 15 minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes is a revolution (360°). 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, so a quarter turn: 90°.

items.q: The pitch of this roof is the angle between the roof and the flat ceiling. It is 25°. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 25° is less than 90°, so the roof pitch is an acute angle.

items.q: Four houses have roof pitches of 15°, 22°, 30° and 40°. Which roof is the steepest?
items.e: The bigger the angle between the roof and the flat ceiling, the steeper the roof. 40° is the largest.

items.q: This skateboard ramp makes an angle of 20° with the ground. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 20° is less than 90°, so it is acute. The small square shows the right angle at the back of the ramp.

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 3 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 spaces between the numbers go around the clock, and each space is 30°. At 3 o’clock the hands are 3 spaces apart: 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle. (15° counts 3 × 5 minutes.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 2 o’clock?
items.e: Each space between two numbers is 30°. At 2 o’clock the hands are 2 spaces apart: 2 × 30° = 60°. (10° counts 2 × 5 minutes.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 5 o’clock?
items.e: Each space between two numbers is 30°. At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. (25° counts 5 × 5 minutes.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 6 o’clock?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point in opposite directions. They make a straight line: 180°. (6 × 30° = 180°.)

items.q: What kind of angle do the hands make at 4 o’clock?
items.e: At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°. That is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: At which time do the hands of a clock make a right angle?
items.e: At 3:00 the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 3: a quarter turn, 90°. At 6:00 they make a straight line, and at 12:00 they are on top of each other.

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn from 7:15 a.m. to 7:45 a.m.?
items.e: In 30 minutes the minute hand goes from 3 to 9, halfway around. The start and end make a straight line: 180°.
The ground is a straight line, so the two angles add up to 180°. 180° − 20° = 160°. (70° comes from 90° − 20°.)
The ground is a straight line: 180° − 35° = 145°. (55° comes from 90° − 35°.)

items.q: A wheelchair ramp makes an angle of 5° with the ground. A skateboard ramp makes 30°. Which is steeper?
items.e: The bigger the angle with the ground, the steeper the ramp. 30° is bigger than 5°, so the skateboard ramp is steeper.
